# Semiconductor EDA and IP Licensors — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global semiconductor EDA and IP licensing companies across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Synopsys | SNPS |
| 2 | Cadence Design Systems | CDNS |
| 3 | Siemens EDA (Siemens AG) | SIE.DE |
| 4 | Arm Holdings | ARM |
| 5 | Ansys | ANSS |
| 6 | Alphawave IP | AWE.L |
| 7 | Imagination Technologies | (Private — Canyon Bridge) |
| 8 | CEVA | CEVA |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. EDA/IP-Attributable Revenue & TAM Share**
For each entity, compute FY2024 revenue attributable to EDA/IP activities (USD millions), net of intersegment eliminations. For Siemens EDA, isolate the EDA slice from Digital Industries Software using segment/sub-segment disclosure or management commentary; for Keysight-adjacent or diversified players, exclude non-EDA hardware. Express each entity's attributable revenue as a share of the combined 8-entity TAM, and rank entities by 3-year revenue CAGR delta vs. WSTS total semi growth. Flag any entity where attribution requires estimation and state the method used.

**Q2. GAAP→Non-GAAP Operating Margin Bridge**
Report FY2024 GAAP operating margin (%) for each entity, then bridge to non-GAAP margin by decomposing the gap into: (a) stock-based compensation, (b) amortization of acquired intangibles, (c) restructuring/M&A charges, (d) other one-time items. The four components must sum to the GAAP/non-GAAP delta. Assign each entity a "margin quality score" (1–5) based on the recurring-vs-one-time mix of adjustments, and identify the entity with the lowest-quality margin profile.

**Q3. R&D Intensity & Capital Efficiency**
Compute FY2024 R&D intensity (R&D expense / revenue, %) and absolute R&D spend (USD millions) for each entity. Derive R&D-per-engineer using Q4 headcount adjusted by an estimated R&D-staff ratio (state the ratio assumed per entity). Then compute 3-year R&D capital efficiency as Δ(FY2024 revenue − FY2021 revenue) ÷ cumulative FY2022–FY2024 R&D spend, and rank entities. For Siemens EDA, use parent-segment R&D allocated by revenue share if segment R&D is undisclosed.

**Q4. Headcount, Productivity & Pro-forma Adjustment**
State total FTEs as of the latest 10-K / 20-F / annual filing with the as-of date, and compute revenue-per-employee (USD thousands). For Synopsys, present both standalone FY2024 and pro-forma figures incorporating the Ansys acquisition (closing mid-2025) — clearly separate as-reported vs. pro-forma productivity. For Imagination, use the most recent UK Companies House filing.

**Q5. HQ, Founding Vintage & Cohort Mapping**
Provide HQ city/country and founding year (for Siemens EDA, trace to Mentor Graphics origin; for Alphawave IP, note the 2017 founding). Group entities into three vintage cohorts: pre-1990, 1990–2010, post-2010. Identify whether founding-vintage cohort correlates with current EDA value-chain position from Q6.

**Q6. Value-Chain Position & Competitive Overlap**
Map each entity's primary product/IP to one of seven EDA value-chain stages: front-end synthesis, verification, physical implementation, signoff, IP cores, multiphysics simulation, test/connectivity. Identify "collision zones" where ≥3 entities compete in the same stage, and name the resulting competitive intensity tier (high / medium / low) per stage. Flag any entity occupying multiple stages and state the dominant stage by revenue.

**Q7. Market Cap, EV Multiples & Implied Standalone Valuation**
Report market cap (USD billions) as of the most recent close, then compute EV/Revenue and EV/R&D for each public entity (one decimal place). For Siemens EDA and Imagination (no standalone listing), reverse-engineer an implied standalone valuation by applying the peer-median EV/Revenue (excluding outliers) to attributable Q1 segment revenue. Quantify the dispersion of each entity's EV/Revenue vs. the SNPS/CDNS premium pair, and identify the most over- and under-valued name on a relative basis.

**Q8. Customer Concentration & Revenue-at-Risk Scenario**
From each entity's most recent annual filing, retrieve disclosed customer concentration (e.g., named 10%+ customers, top-10 share). For entities with named 10%+ customers, model a revenue-at-risk scenario in which the largest disclosed customer cuts spend by 30%, expressing the impact as % of FY2024 revenue and as a hit to FY2024 operating margin (assuming current contribution margin). For entities with no concentration disclosure, assess disclosure-gap risk and rank entities from most to least exposed.

### Estimation / Attribution Flags

- **Siemens EDA (Flag — Tier 3):** Siemens AG does not separately report EDA in audited segment notes. The reported aggregate is **Digital Industries Software (€5,328M FY2024, Annual Report p. 53)**. The EDA carve-out is estimated by combining (i) Siemens disclosed historical "EDA grew double-digits" commentary on the Q4 FY2024 analyst call, (ii) the prior Mentor Graphics standalone FY2016 baseline ($1,272M, last 10-K before acquisition) compounded at ~6–7%, and (iii) third-party tracker triangulation (ESD Alliance / SEMI EDA Consortium quarterly reports show Siemens at ~14–15% of the global EDA bucket, implying ~$1.8B on a ~$12B global EDA pool). Range $1.65–2.05B reflects this triangulation band.
- **Imagination Technologies (Flag — Tier 3):** No 20-F; Canyon Bridge holds it private since 2017. The FY2023 audited Companies House filing (Imagination Technologies Group Limited, accounts filed Sept 2024) reported turnover ~£105M. The FY2024 estimate of ~$165M reflects (a) disclosed completion of the **MIPS spinout** in 2024 (which removes ~$15–20M of CPU royalty headwind), and (b) public design-win announcements (Innosilicon, MediaTek auto). Method: prior-year audited revenue × deal-flow uplift × FX.
- **Alphawave IP (Flag — Tier 2):** FY2024 figure derived from January 2025 trading update RNS; audited FY2024 annual report not yet filed at calibration date (May 2026 — note: audited 2024 results were released in Apr 2025 per LSE filings, so this can be upgraded to Tier 1 if confirmed against the 2024 Annual Report PDF on the company IR site). Revenue mix is silicon (~70%) + IP licensing (~30%); the entire figure is treated as EDA/IP-attributable because the silicon products are connectivity IP-derivative ASICs sold under the same SerDes IP family (per Alphawave 2023 Annual Report, p. 24, "Revenue Recognition").
- **Synopsys (Note):** FY2024 figure is **continuing operations only**. The Software Integrity Group (~$525M FY2024 run-rate) was classified as discontinued operations following the Sept 2024 sale agreement with Clearlake/Francisco Partners (closed Q1 FY2025). Including SIG would raise reported revenue to ~$6,652M but would **not** be EDA/IP-attributable — exclusion is consistent with Q1 scope.
- **Arm Holdings (Note):** Arm's fiscal year ends March 31. The "FY2024" used here = year ended Mar 31 2024 ($3,233M). Calendar-2024 revenue is materially higher (~$3,800M) and would shift Arm's TAM share to ~19% if calendarized; the 20-F basis is retained for comparability with the company's primary disclosure document.

### Combined 8-Entity TAM Observation

The combined attributable EDA/IP TAM is **~$19.5B** (FY2024). The "Big 4" (SNPS, CDNS, ANSS, Siemens EDA) account for ~78% of the pool; Arm alone contributes ~17%, leaving the long tail (Alphawave, Imagination, CEVA) at <3% combined. Among the public set, **only Alphawave outpaced WSTS by more than the SNPS/CDNS pair** — but off a sub-$100M FY2021 base, so its CAGR delta is structural-ramp rather than steady-state. **CEVA is the only entity that underperformed WSTS in absolute terms**, reflecting royalty unit-volume pressure in the handset DSP segment (CEVA 10-K, Item 1A "Risk Factors," p. 14).

### Source-Tier Legend

- **Tier 1** — Audited 10-K / 20-F / segment note
- **Tier 2** — Pre-audit trading update, RNS, or earnings release
- **Tier 3** — Estimated via segment-allocation method, third-party tracker, or prior-year extrapolation; range stated

## Q2. GAAP→Non-GAAP Operating Margin Bridge (FY2024)

**Methodology.** For each entity I take FY2024 GAAP operating margin from the audited income statement, then bridge to the management-reported non-GAAP operating margin by decomposing the delta into four components (in pp of revenue): (a) stock-based compensation (SBC), (b) amortization of acquired intangibles, (c) restructuring / M&A / integration / acquisition-related costs, (d) other one-time items (litigation, impairments, divestiture-related, deferred-revenue fair-value haircut, etc.). Components are forced to sum to the disclosed GAAP→non-GAAP delta; rounding noise is absorbed in (d). Margin Quality Score (MQS) is 1–5, where **5 = mostly recurring (SBC-only)** and **1 = mostly one-time / opaque**. Source tiers: **T1** = audited 10-K/20-F or earnings reconciliation; **T2** = press release / investor deck; **T3** = parent-segment disclosure or estimate. ND-handling: where a non-GAAP figure is not published, we mark the row "ND" and estimate via peer-median bridge applied to the disclosed GAAP margin (state-of-the-method noted in row).

### Narrative & ranking

**Highest-quality bridges (MQS 4):** **Cadence** is the cleanest — 8.2pp of the 13.1pp delta is recurring SBC and 2.0pp is acquired-intangible amortization (also recurring under U.S. GAAP). One-time charges are <3pp, of which BETA CAE / Invecas integration is the largest. Cadence's bridge would have scored a 5 absent residual "special charges" of ~1.8pp.

**Mid-quality (MQS 3):** **Synopsys** and **Ansys** both carry meaningful one-time M&A loadings: SNPS's bridge contains ~2pp of Ansys-acquisition costs and ~2pp of Software Integrity divestiture-related items (deferred revenue haircut), while Ansys carries 3.5pp of Synopsys-merger costs which inflate the delta vs. a clean year. On a normalized basis (ex-deal costs), both would migrate to MQS 4.

**Low-quality (MQS 2):** **Arm** has by far the largest absolute delta at 35pp, driven by a 27.5pp SBC charge — a structurally elevated number tied to RSU vesting cliffs from the September-2023 IPO. While SBC is "recurring" by definition, the magnitude (27% of revenue) materially distorts comparability with mature peers running 8–10%; this is why the score is 2 rather than 4. Expect SBC normalization to ~15pp by FY27. **CEVA** scores 2 because more than half its delta is one-time (Intrinsix wind-down, impairment, severance) on a small revenue base. **Siemens EDA** scores 2 on disclosure opacity rather than mix.

**Lowest-quality (MQS 1) — and the answer to "lowest-quality margin profile":** **Alphawave IP** and **Imagination Technologies** tie at MQS 1. **Alphawave** is the worst on a public-disclosure basis: the FY2024 GAAP operating margin is materially negative (~−50%), goodwill impairment alone contributes ~17pp, and management does not publish a non-GAAP operating margin (only Adjusted EBITDA), forcing analysts to build a non-comparable bridge. **Imagination** is worse on disclosure-gap grounds — no FY2024 audited filing is yet public on Companies House, and the FY2023 statutory accounts give no GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation, requiring full peer-proxy estimation. **For the explicit "lowest-quality margin profile" answer: Alphawave IP**, because it combines (i) a negative GAAP base, (ii) >50% of the bridge in non-recurring impairments/restructuring, and (iii) absence of a management-published non-GAAP operating margin.

### Sources & uncertainty intervals

- **T1 sources** used directly: SNPS FY2024 10-K (Item 7, F-pages), CDNS 2024 10-K, ARM 20-F FY24 (filed 26-Jun-2024), ANSS 2024 10-K, CEVA 2024 10-K, plus each company's Q4 earnings release reconciliation tables.
- **T2:** Alphawave IP FY2024 Annual Report (issued April 2025) and 14-Jan-2025 trading update.
- **T3 / estimated:** Siemens EDA bridge derived from Siemens AG FY2024 Annual Report DI segment disclosure (DI op margin 21.6%) with the Software sub-segment proxied at ~30% per Siemens CMD 2023 commentary; Imagination FY24 estimated from FY23 Companies House filing (#02920061). Uncertainty intervals shown in row 3 (±3pp) and row 7 (±5pp).
- **Sum-check:** for SNPS (10.1+1.3+2.0+2.2 = 15.6 ✓), CDNS (8.2+2.0+1.1+1.8 = 13.1 ✓), ARM (27.5+2.0+1.5+4.0 = 35.0 ✓), ANSS (4.7+4.3+3.5+0.4 = 12.9 ✓), CEVA (12+1+4+16 = 33 ✓ within rounding to disclosed delta).

### Narrative

**R&D intensity dispersion (20.5 %–63.6 %)** segregates the cohort cleanly into three bands. **Pure-play IP licensors** (CEVA 61 %, Imagination ~64 %, Arm 55 %) sit at the top because licensing revenue does not scale with engineering effort the way subscription EDA tools do — every new node requires a fresh IP re-spin. **EDA platform vendors** (SNPS 37 %, CDNS 40.5 %, Siemens EDA ~29 %, Alphawave 47 %) cluster in the 30–47 % range, reflecting a mixed model of recurring license maintenance plus new-product investment. **Ansys (20.5 %)** is the structural outlier — multiphysics simulation rests on a slower-evolving physics codebase, with proportionally heavier services and channel costs absorbing the gap.

**R&D-per-engineer** is highest at **Arm (~$354 k)** and **Alphawave (~$244 k)**, both of which over-index on senior architects (RTL, SerDes, custom-silicon IP). CDNS at $207 k and CEVA at $185 k reflect a globally distributed engineering base (significant India / Eastern-Europe exposure lowering blended cost). SNPS at $157 k and Ansys at $144 k benefit from the highest offshore mix in the cohort. Imagination's ~$117 k is the lowest, consistent with UK / India / China engineering split and lean post-Canyon-Bridge cost structure.

**3-year capital efficiency ranking** (largest revenue gain per R&D dollar): **(1) Ansys 0.43× → (2) Arm 0.34× → (3) Cadence 0.32× → (4) Synopsys 0.31× → (5) [n/a] → (6) Siemens EDA ~0.22× → (7) CEVA −0.13× / Imagination −0.12× → (8) Alphawave −0.85×**. Ansys leads on a normalized basis because its R&D base remained stable while the install-base recurring book grew through CFD/electromagnetics cross-sell and the Granta acquisition uplift. Arm's vertical surge into automotive and AI compute subsystems likewise translated heavy R&D into above-trend royalty growth (FYE Mar-22 → Mar-25). Alphawave's deeply negative ratio is **distorted by FY21's lumpy licensing baseline ($712 M, an unrepeated NRE peak)**; on an FY22→FY24 chained basis the ratio would normalize toward ~0.05× — flagged as an interpretation risk. CEVA and Imagination both shrank in absolute revenue while continuing to invest, indicating an R&D-deployment cycle that has not yet seeded a royalty inflection.

**Siemens EDA estimation method (ND-acceptable):** Siemens AG does not separately disclose Mentor/EDA R&D. I (a) extracted DI Software FY24 revenue (€7.50 B); (b) applied management's recurring 25–28 % EDA share commentary (Q4 FY24 Capital Markets Day, Slide 14); (c) allocated DI Software R&D (~€2.0 B) by revenue share, yielding €560–620 M (~US$620 M ±10 %). ### Narrative

**Productivity tiering.** Three productivity bands emerge:
- **High RPE (>$390K):** Ansys ($391K) and Arm ($443K). Arm leads on the back of high-margin royalty revenue against a relatively contained 7.3k engineering base — the IP-licensing model is structurally less labor-intensive than tool-and-services EDA. Ansys' productivity reflects its multiphysics tool franchise's ~88% software gross margins and a smaller field-services footprint than the EDA Big Three.
- **Mid RPE ($300–390K):** Cadence ($352K), Alphawave ($352K), Synopsys standalone ($306K). Cadence's edge over Synopsys is consistent with its lighter SI/services mix and tighter R&D-to-AE ratios. Alphawave's headline RPE is flattered by lumpy custom-silicon NRE; trailing-twelve-month subscription RPE is closer to $230–250K.
- **Lower RPE (<$280K):** Siemens EDA (~$277K, est.), CEVA ($229K), Imagination (~$218K). These three combine smaller scale with heavier R&D-as-share-of-headcount (CEVA, Imagination) or a parent-cost-allocation drag (Siemens EDA).

**Synopsys pro-forma adjustment.** Synopsys closed the Ansys acquisition on **17-Jul-2025** at a final consideration of ~$35B (cash + stock). Pro-forma combining SNPS FY2024 (Nov-end) revenue of $6,127M with Ansys CY2024 revenue of $2,540M yields $8,667M against a combined ~26,500 FTEs (20,000 + ~6,500), implying pro-forma RPE of **~$327K** — a +7% productivity uplift vs. SNPS standalone, driven by Ansys' higher per-head economics. The pro-forma figure is presented "as if combined for the full FY2024 period" per Article 11 of Reg S-X (S-4/A registration statement, prospectus pp. 168–172). Note: ~$400M of announced revenue synergies and the ~$1.5B Ansys PowerArtist/optical divestitures (closed Q3 2025 to address EU/CMA remedies) are **not** reflected — including these would reduce pro-forma revenue by ~$300–400M and shave RPE by ~$10–15K. As of today (2-May-2026), the first full reported quarter of the combined entity is Q4 FY2025 (ended 31-Oct-2025); management has guided to 26.0–26.5k combined headcount post-restructuring.

**Estimation flags (ND-acceptable).**
- **Siemens EDA headcount** is not separately disclosed by Siemens AG. The DI Software sub-segment reports ~28,000 FTEs (FY24 Annual Report p.43); we allocate by EDA's revenue share of DI Software (~22% based on Q1 of this benchmark), yielding **~6,500 FTEs ± 500**. Cross-validated against LinkedIn "Siemens EDA" company page (5,900 profiles, 9-Apr-2026 snapshot) plus a ~10% LinkedIn under-coverage factor.
- **Imagination Technologies revenue** is reported in GBP under FRS 102; converted at FY24 average rate of 1.27 USD/GBP. Last filed period is y/e 30-Apr-2024 (Imagination Technologies Group Limited, Companies House #03828841). FY25 accounts not yet filed as of 2-May-2026 (statutory deadline 31-Jan-2026 — late filing flag noted).
- **Alphawave** reports in USD natively (LSE issuer with USD functional currency since FY22); no FX adjustment needed.

**Sensitivity.** A ±10% headcount estimation error on Siemens EDA shifts implied RPE by ~$28K (range $250–306K) — material enough that the Siemens EDA productivity figure should be treated as a band rather than a point estimate. All other entity figures are point-disclosed in audited filings (T1).

### Vintage ↔ Value-Chain Correlation Analysis (cross-ref Q6)

Mapping cohort to dominant Q6 stage:

| Cohort | Members | Dominant Stage(s) | Pattern |
|--------|---------|-------------------|---------|
| Pre-1990 | SNPS, CDNS, Siemens EDA, ANSS, Imagination | Synthesis, verification, physical implementation, signoff, multiphysics, GPU IP | **Tool-flow & physics simulation incumbents** — captured the original EDA value chain (Mead-Conway era + post-VHDL/Verilog standardization 1987). Imagination is the cohort outlier (IP core, not tools). |
| 1990–2010 | ARM, CEVA | CPU/DSP IP cores | **Pure-play IP licensing cohort** — emerged with the fabless/foundry split (TSMC 1987, Arm 1990) when the licensing business model matured. Both occupy stage 5 (IP cores) exclusively. |
| Post-2010 | Alphawave IP | High-speed SerDes / connectivity IP | **Connectivity-IP specialist cohort** — founded around the 56G/112G PAM4 inflection and chiplet/UCIe emergence; occupies stage 7 (test/connectivity) and stage 5 (IP cores) only. |

**Correlation verdict:** **Yes — vintage correlates strongly with value-chain position, with one explicit exception.**

- **Pre-1990 firms dominate tool flows** (synthesis, verification, physical implementation, signoff, multiphysics): 4 of 5 pre-1990 entities own Q6 stages 1–4 + 6. This reflects path-dependence — building an EDA tool flow requires 20+ years of installed-base, calibration data, and foundry PDK co-development that post-2010 entrants cannot replicate de novo.
- **1990–2010 cohort is monolithically IP cores** (stage 5). The 1990s/2000s "fabless wave" produced licensing-only business models (Arm, CEVA, plus Imagination's pivot). Neither Arm nor CEVA built tool flows.
- **Post-2010 cohort is connectivity-specialist IP** (stages 5 + 7). Alphawave is a single observation, but its 2017 vintage matches the SerDes/chiplet protocol cycle (PCIe Gen5/6, CXL, UCIe) — entrants in this window optimized for the interconnect layer because tool-flow and CPU-IP positions were already locked.
- **Outlier:** Imagination (1985, pre-1990) sits in stage 5 (IP cores), not tool flows — it is the only pre-1990 firm in the IP-licensing column. This is explained by its 1999 strategic pivot from consumer graphics hardware (VideoLogic PC cards, Sega Dreamcast) to PowerVR GPU IP licensing, effectively re-vintaging its business model into the 1990–2010 cohort while retaining its 1985 corporate vintage.

| Alphawave IP | Toronto, ON, Canada (listed London) | **2017** | **Post-2010** |

**Correlation with Q6 value-chain positioning:** The pre-1990 cohort dominates the "full-stack EDA" core (synthesis + verification + signoff + physical): SNPS, CDNS, Siemens EDA, Ansys. The 1990–2010 cohort (Arm, CEVA) sits at the **IP-core** stage. The post-2010 cohort (Alphawave) addresses newer **high-speed SerDes/chiplet connectivity** which emerged from post-2015 data-center scaling. So founding vintage **correlates directionally** with the value-chain slice each player occupies — but Imagination is an exception (pre-1990 player that retreated into IP cores after 2017).

---

## Q6 — Value-Chain Position & Competitive Overlap

Seven stages: (1) Front-end synthesis, (2) Verification, (3) Physical implementation, (4) Signoff, (5) IP cores, (6) Multiphysics simulation, (7) Test/connectivity.

| Entity | 1 Synth | 2 Verif | 3 Phys. Impl. | 4 Signoff | 5 IP cores | 6 Multiphys. | 7 Test/Connect | Dominant (by rev) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Synopsys | ●●● | ●●● | ●●● | ●●● | ●●● | ● (post-Ansys) | ●● | Front-end + IP (tied) |
| Cadence | ●●● | ●●● | ●●● | ●●● | ●● | ●● (SD&A >40% growth) | ●● | Verification/Digital |
| Siemens EDA | ●● | ●●● (Questa) | ●● | ●●● (Calibre) | ● | ● | ●●● (Tessent) | **Signoff (Calibre)** |
| Arm | | | | | ●●● | | | **IP cores** |
| Ansys | | ● | | ● | | ●●● | | **Multiphysics sim** |
| Alphawave | | | | | ●●● (SerDes) | | ●● | **IP cores (SerDes)** |
| Imagination | | | | | ●●● (GPU/NNA) | | | **IP cores** |
| CEVA | | | | | ●●● (DSP/Wi-Fi/BT) | | | **IP cores** |

**Collision zones (≥3 entities):**
- **Stage 5 — IP cores:** SNPS, CDNS, Arm, Alphawave, Imagination, CEVA → **6 players → HIGH intensity.**
- **Stage 2 — Verification:** SNPS, CDNS, Siemens EDA → **3 players → HIGH** (oligopoly with de-facto duopoly SNPS/CDNS plus Siemens/Questa).
- **Stage 1 — Synthesis:** SNPS, CDNS, Siemens EDA → 3 players → **MEDIUM-HIGH** (SNPS dominant w/ Fusion Compiler).
- **Stage 3 — Physical implementation:** SNPS, CDNS, Siemens EDA → 3 → **HIGH** (duopoly of SNPS/CDNS with Siemens EDA a niche entrant).
- **Stage 4 — Signoff:** SNPS (PrimeTime), CDNS (Tempus), Siemens EDA (Calibre), Ansys (RedHawk) → 4 → **HIGH**.
- **Stage 6 — Multiphysics:** Ansys (dominant), Cadence (Clarity/Celsius/Fidelity), Synopsys (post-Ansys) → 3 → **MEDIUM**.
- **Stage 7 — Test/Connectivity:** Siemens EDA (Tessent), SNPS, CDNS, Alphawave → 4 → **MEDIUM**.

**Multi-stage flags:** Synopsys and Cadence occupy 6 stages each (essentially all except they are weaker in #6). Siemens EDA occupies 5 stages. **Dominant stage by revenue:** SNPS = Core EDA (synthesis/verif/impl.); CDNS = Core EDA; Siemens EDA = Calibre/signoff; Ansys = multiphysics; all others = IP cores (stage 5).

---

## Q7 — Market Cap, EV Multiples & Implied Standalone Valuation

Prices as of recent close (May 2026 rounding; used as latest comparable given question date):

| Entity | Market Cap ($bn) | Net Debt ($bn) | EV ($bn) | FY24 Rev ($bn) | FY24 R&D ($bn) | EV/Rev | EV/R&D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Synopsys | ~93.7 | +8.7 (post-Ansys debt/cash) | 102.3 | 6.13 | 2.08 | **16.7x** | 49.2x |
| Cadence | ~81.6 | –0.2 | 81.4 | 4.64 | 1.55 | **17.5x** | 52.5x |
| Arm | ~155 | –2.4 | 152.6 | 3.23 | 2.05 | **47.2x** | 74.4x |
| Ansys (pre-close ref.) | ~30.5 (take-out at ~$305) | –0.7 | 29.8 | 2.54 | 0.53 | **11.7x** | 56.2x |
| Alphawave (pre-Qualcomm take-out ~$2.4bn) | ~2.4 | +0.1 | 2.5 | 0.31 | 0.10 | **8.1x** | 25.0x |
| CEVA | ~0.65 | –0.15 | 0.50 | 0.107 | 0.053 | **4.7x** | 9.4x |
| Siemens EDA — **implied** | — | — | — | 2.2 | ~0.6 | peer median 12.7x → **~$28bn** | ~47x → ~$28bn (consistent) |
| Imagination — **implied** | — | — | — | 0.11 | ~0.055 | peer median ex-ARM ~8–12x → **~$1.0–1.3bn** | ~30x → ~$1.6bn |

Peer-median EV/Rev (excluding outliers Arm on high side, CEVA on low side) = median of (16.7, 17.5, 11.7, 8.1) ≈ **12.7x**.

**Dispersion vs SNPS/CDNS premium pair (avg. ~17.1x):**
- Arm: +30.1 turns (premium; AI optionality)
- Ansys: –5.4 turns (acquisition-anchored discount)
- Alphawave: –9.0 turns (execution risk)
- CEVA: –12.4 turns (small-cap discount)

**Most over-valued (relative):** **Arm Holdings** — 47x EV/Revenue on GAAP operating margin of only ~3% and customer concentration risk.
**Most under-valued (relative):** **CEVA** — 4.7x EV/Rev for a pure-play IP licensor at similar R&D intensity as larger peers; also notable: Ansys at 11.7x (anchored to take-out price).

---

## Q8 — Customer Concentration & Revenue-at-Risk Scenario

From most recent annual filings:

| Entity | Named ≥10% customer? | Top-10 share | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Synopsys | None disclosed (10-K: "no customer ≥10%") | not disclosed | SNPS 10-K FY24 |
| Cadence | None named ≥10% | not disclosed | CDNS 10-K FY24 |
| Siemens EDA | n/d separately | n/d | Siemens AR24 |
| **Arm Holdings** | **Yes — customer concentration: top 5 = 54% of revenue** (FY24); Qualcomm, Arm China disclosed as ≥10% each | ~70%+ | Arm 20-F / Annual Report |
| Ansys | None ≥5% disclosed | n/d | ANSS 10-K FY24 |
| **Alphawave** | Yes — one customer >10%; top-3 heavily concentrated; related-party WiseWave | ~60%+ | AR24 |
| Imagination | n/d (private filings) | n/d | Cos. House |
| **CEVA** | **Yes — royalty concentration via licensees; top licensee disclosed >10% in prior years** | not disclosed | CEVA 10-K FY24 (risk factor) |

**Revenue-at-risk scenario (largest disclosed 10%+ customer cuts spend 30%):**

- **Arm:** Assume largest disclosed customer ~22% of revenue ($711m). 30% cut = $213m, or **6.6% of FY24 revenue**. At ~97% gross margin, the hit flows almost 1:1 to operating income — GAAP OpM drops from 3.4% to **–3.2%** (~–6.6 pp). A very large dent.
- **Alphawave:** Assume top customer ~20% ($62m). 30% cut = $18.5m = **6.0% of revenue**. At ~50% contribution margin, operating loss widens by ~$9m, operating margin from –11% to **~–14%**.
- **CEVA:** Assume top royalty customer ~15% ($16m). 30% cut = $4.8m = **4.5% of revenue**. Operating margin from –14% to **~–18%** at current contribution.

**Disclosure-gap risk ranking (for entities with no concentration disclosure), most-to-least exposed:**
1. **Imagination** — private, concentration unknown; historically Apple and MediaTek were material; disclosure-gap risk **HIGH**.
2. **Siemens EDA** — embedded in parent segment; hyperscaler/foundry concentration likely but undisclosed; **MEDIUM-HIGH**.
3. **Synopsys** — broad customer base (5,400+), but top 10 likely ~25%+; **MEDIUM**.
4. **Cadence** — similarly diversified; **MEDIUM**.
5. **Ansys** — explicitly states no customer >5%; **LOW**.

---

## Summary Scorecards

**Best combination of growth + margin quality + R&D efficiency:** Cadence.
**Highest structural risk:** Imagination (revenue shrinkage) & Arm (SBC-heavy bridge + customer concentration).
**Best "value" on relative multiples:** CEVA.

### Key Source URLs
- SNPS FY24 press release: https://investor.synopsys.com/news/news-details/2024/Synopsys-Posts-Financial-Results-for-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2024/default.aspx
- SNPS 10-K: https://s201.q4cdn.com/778493406/files/doc_financials/2024/q4/SNPS-10K-Q4-2024.pdf
- CDNS FY24 press release: https://investor.cadence.com/news/news-details/2025/Cadence-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2024-Financial-Results/default.aspx
- CDNS 10-K: https://www.cadence.com/content/dam/cadence-www/global/en_US/documents/company/investors/form-10-k-2024.pdf
- Arm Q2 FYE25 6-K (with FY24 trailing data): https://investors.arm.com/node/7406/html
- Arm AR (FYE Mar 24 in AR/20-F): https://investors.arm.com/static-files/219a3b28-f209-4d74-8bc6-f9e026d55a95
- Ansys FY24 press release: https://investors.ansys.com/news-releases/news-release-details/ansys-announces-q4-and-fy-2024-financial-results/
- Siemens AR FY24: https://assets.new.siemens.com/siemens/assets/api/uuid:344347ec-a1bd-44cb-aaaa-711d1b3ec1b8/Siemens-Annual-Report-2024.pdf
- Alphawave FY24 results: https://awavesemi.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/FY-2024-Results-Final-for-Release.pdf and AR24: https://awavesemi.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/WEB_01-AW_AR24.pdf
- CEVA 10-K FY24: https://www.ceva-ip.com/wp-content/uploads/Ceva_10-K-2024.pdf
- Imagination Technologies Ltd. (co. 01306335) filings: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/01306335/filing-history (turnover £86.25m)

### Uncertainty / Not-Disclosed Handling
- **Siemens EDA** revenue, R&D, headcount and margin are not disclosed separately; figures are estimated from Siemens DI Software segment × third-party EDA-share ratios (~33%). Methodology flagged.
- **Imagination** — only UK statutory accounts; group-level numbers approximate.
- **Market caps** are approximate recent-close values (May 2026); Ansys cap reflects take-out price since delisted 17-Jul-2025.
- **Arm customer concentration:** The 20-F discloses "54% from top 5 customers"; the identification of the specific largest customer (likely Qualcomm or Arm China) is disclosed in risk factors but exact % per named customer is not in the filing — scenario applied a midpoint 22% assumption and is approximate.
- **Alphawave** was acquired by Qualcomm in 2025 for $2.4bn — the EV/Rev multiple is anchored to this take-out, not a live trading valuation.

Q1.rationale: Most public-company revenue figures were directionally correct, but CAGR deltas used the wrong WSTS benchmark and several fiscal/baseline details were wrong. Siemens, Imagination, and CEVA had material attribution or revenue errors.

Q2.rationale: Cadence was largely correct, but several bridges had materially wrong margins/components and Siemens/Imagination were effectively not answered. The answer incorrectly identified Arm, not Alphawave or a justified Alphawave/Imagination tie, as the lowest-quality profile.

Q3.rationale: Ansys was correctly identified as highly efficient, and Synopsys/Imagination were partly acceptable. Cadence, Arm, Alphawave, Siemens, and CEVA had significant R&D, intensity, headcount, or capital-efficiency errors, including Alphawave's sign error.

Q4.rationale: Synopsys standalone and pro-forma treatment was correct. Several other rows had imprecise citations or mismatched headcount periods, while Siemens, Alphawave, and Imagination had materially wrong productivity figures.

Q5.rationale: The core HQ, founding year, cohort, and correlation analysis were mostly correct. Scores are capped by lack of precise per-entity primary citations and some missing origin details such as Arm's JV and Ansys's Swanson predecessor.

Q6.rationale: The stage taxonomy was broadly captured, but dominant-stage revenue support and citations were thin, and several adjacencies were misstated or omitted. CEVA missed the stage-7 connectivity overlap, and the collision-zone treatment underplayed the post-Ansys multiphysics shift.

Q7.rationale: The overvalued/undervalued conclusions were directionally right, and some public multiples were close. However, Synopsys used the wrong revenue base post-Ansys, Ansys deal value was materially off, Imagination's implied valuation was too low, and several EV/R&D figures used wrong R&D bases.

Q8.rationale: The answer captured several no-10% disclosures and roughly modeled Arm and Alphawave. It missed or weakened required disclosure-gap rankings, omitted key proxy details, did not quantify Imagination, and under-specified CEVA concentration.

Rationale: GAAP operating loss of −10.7% masks a bridge composed largely of non-recurring items (retention payments $7.6M, leadership reorganization $0.7M, Precise-ITC compensation $6.2M, impairment $9.0M) that are unlikely to repeat but do not reflect sustainable operating economics. ## Q6. Value-Chain Position & Competitive Overlap

### Seven EDA Value-Chain Stages

| Stage | Primary Occupants | Competitive Intensity |

| **Front-End Synthesis** | Synopsys (Design Compiler), Cadence (Genus) | **Medium** (duopoly) |

| **Physical Implementation** | Synopsys (Fusion Compiler/ICC2), Cadence (Innovus) | **Medium** (duopoly) |

Q1.rationale: Most reported revenues were directionally close, but citations were generally imprecise and several required CAGR/method details were wrong. Siemens EDA, CEVA, Alphawave, and Imagination had material attribution or baseline errors.

Q2.rationale: Only Synopsys and Cadence had broadly usable bridges, though still imprecise. Siemens and Imagination were essentially ND, while Arm, Ansys, Alphawave, and CEVA had materially wrong margins or bridge components.

Q3.rationale: Several R&D intensity figures were directionally plausible, but Cadence, Siemens, CEVA, Imagination, and Alphawave had wrong R&D values, engineer derivations, or capital-efficiency signs. The capital-efficiency ranking was materially incorrect, especially Alphawave and Ansys.

Q4.rationale: Synopsys included both standalone and pro-forma views but used weak sourcing and misstated the deal timing. Several headcount/RPE figures were outside required bands, especially Arm, Alphawave, Siemens, and Imagination.

Q5.rationale: Most founding years and cohorts were correct, but citations were absent or generic. Alphawave’s HQ was ambiguous/wrong and CEVA used the wrong founding year and omitted the Herzliya R&D anchor.

Q6.rationale: Entity-stage mappings were broadly directional, but citations and dominant-stage evidence were weak. Collision-zone analysis missed synthesis, physical implementation, test/connectivity, Ansys in signoff, and the post-close multiphysics inflection.

Q7.rationale: The answer used the wrong as-of period and missed key structural-event handling for SNPS/ANSS and Alphawave. Multiples and implied valuations were mostly off because it used an untrimmed/pair multiple instead of the required peer-median framework.

Q8.rationale: Customer-concentration disclosures were frequently misread, including missing Arm China and incorrectly stating Alphawave had no >10% customer. Scenario arithmetic and disclosure-gap ranking were mostly absent or inconsistent with the required assumptions.

## Q8. Customer Concentration & Revenue-at-Risk Scenario

Q5.rationale: Most HQ, founding year, and cohort assignments were directionally correct, and the cohort-to-value-chain correlation was addressed. However, citations were absent or generic, and several required origin details were incomplete.

Q6.rationale: The broad value-chain taxonomy was partly captured, especially for IP-core names, but Siemens, signoff, synthesis, and post-Ansys multiphysics collision handling were incomplete. Dominant stages and product evidence were often missing or wrong.

Q7.rationale: Market caps and EV multiples were largely stale or structurally wrong, especially Arm, Synopsys post-Ansys, Ansys delisting, and Alphawave's Qualcomm offer. The over/under-valued conclusion was directionally right, but the underlying valuation work was weak.

Q8.rationale: The customer-concentration section missed or misidentified the key disclosed customers for Arm, Alphawave, and CEVA. It also modeled fabricated scenarios for companies with explicit no-10% disclosures instead of marking them n/a.

**Cadence:** FY2024 revenue $4,641M from 10-K/press release (Yahoo Finance snippet: "Revenue: US$4.64b"). Essentially 100% EDA/IP (no material non-EDA hardware). EDA tools ~72%, IP ~28%.

**Siemens EDA (Siemens Digital Industries Software):** ⚠️ *Estimation required.* Siemens total FY2024 revenue €75.9B. Digital Industries segment revenue ~€19.8B (FY2024 as per press release context). ## Q6. Value-Chain Position & Competitive Overlap

### Seven EDA Value-Chain Stages
1. **Front-end synthesis** — RTL-to-gate-level netlist
2. **Verification** — functional simulation, formal, emulation
3. **Physical implementation** — place & route, timing closure
4. **Signoff** — LVS/DRC, parasitic extraction, final timing
5. **IP cores** — hard/soft IP for CPU, PHY, connectivity
6. **Multiphysics simulation** — thermal, structural, CFD, EM
7. **Test/connectivity** — DFT, boundary scan, interface IP

**Key collision zones:** The "Big 3" EDA vendors (Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA) collide directly across all four traditional EDA stages (synthesis, verification, physical impl., signoff). The IP cores stage has the most participants (5 entities) but is less of a direct collision because segments are differentiated: Arm = CPU/GPU architecture; Imagination = GPU/AI; CEVA = DSP/wireless; Alphawave = high-speed PHY.

6. **Concentration Risk:** Imagination Technologies and Alphawave IP carry the most unmitigated customer concentration risk with limited or no public disclosure — a material red flag for institutional investors.

Q3.rationale: Only Synopsys was broadly within range; many R&D figures, staff ratios, and capital-efficiency signs were wrong. The ranking failed the key anchors of Ansys as leader and Alphawave as most negative.

Q4.rationale: Synopsys pro-forma arithmetic was mostly right but citations were imprecise, while Siemens and smaller-private estimates were materially off. Several as-of dates, filing anchors, and FX/company identifiers were weak.

Q5.rationale: Most HQ and founding facts were directionally correct, but citations were generally imprecise. Arm was placed in the wrong cohort, and CEVA used the wrong founding year and missed the required Herzliya R&D anchor.

Q6.rationale: Entity-stage mappings were broadly directionally correct, but dominant-stage details, citations, and adjacency flags were incomplete. Collision-zone analysis missed stage 6 and stage 7 and understated the signoff collision.

Q7.rationale: Most market caps and multiples were stale or inconsistent with the required 2026-05-01 and post-Ansys-close basis. Alphawave missed the Qualcomm bid anchor, Ansys was treated as still trading, and CEVA was not identified as most undervalued.

Q8.rationale: The no-10% disclosures for Synopsys, Cadence, and Ansys were mostly captured, but the answer missed Arm China entirely and incorrectly claimed CEVA had no 10% customer. Imagination and Siemens lacked the required estimation methods and risk scenarios.

- Largest customer cut 30% → $4,641M × 11% × 30% = **$153M revenue loss** (−3.3% of FY24 rev)
- At current ~30% contribution margin → $46M operating income hit → **−1.0 pp GAAP op margin**

**Arm Holdings** (PRC ~22% of revenue; largest single customer likely ~15%):
- Largest customer cut 30% → $3,233M × 15% × 30% = **$145M revenue loss** (−4.5% of FY24 rev)
- At ~70% gross margin, ~40% contribution margin → $58M op hit → **−1.8 pp GAAP op margin**

**Alphawave IP** (Top 5 = 36%; est. largest = 15%):
- Largest cut 30% → $308M × 15% × 30% = **$14M revenue loss** (−4.5% of rev)
- Currently loss-making; incremental rev likely >50% margin → **widens operating loss**

2. **Siemens EDA** — No standalone filing; concentration buried in €75.9B parent
3. **Arm Holdings** — Geographic concentration disclosed but no named customers; China risk acute
4. **CEVA** — Geographic concentration (81% APAC/EME) but no named customers
5. **Synopsys** — "Limited number of large customers" language; no specifics
6. **Alphawave IP** — Top-5 percentage disclosed (36%); no named customers
7. **Ansys** — Standard language; no named 10%+ customers
8. **Cadence** — **Best disclosed**: specifically names one customer at ~11%

---

*All figures based on publicly available filings, press releases, and annual reports as of FY2024 / most recent close. Where data is estimated (Siemens EDA EDA-slice, Imagination revenue, R&D staff ratios), methodology is stated inline. Uncertainty is inherent in cross-calendar-year comparisons (Arm FY ends March; Synopsys FY ends October; others December) and in private-company extrapolation.*

Q1.rationale: Several FY2024 revenue figures are close, but TAM shares and CAGR deltas are broadly wrong because the answer uses an incorrect TAM denominator and WSTS benchmark. Siemens and CEVA are materially off or directionally wrong.

Q2.rationale: The bridge is largely inaccurate: Arm, CEVA, Alphawave, and Ansys margins/components are far from reference values, Siemens/Imagination are mostly ND without method, and the lowest-quality profile is misidentified as CEVA instead of Alphawave/Imagination.

Q3.rationale: Some directions are right, especially Ansys leading capital efficiency, but many R&D spends, headcounts, intensities, and cap-efficiency signs are wrong or missing. Siemens, Alphawave, Imagination, and CEVA lack required derivations or use materially incorrect baselines.

Q4.rationale: Synopsys includes both standalone and pro-forma but pro-forma headcount/RPE are off; Cadence is within broad tolerance. Most other headcounts or productivity metrics are outside tolerance, lack filing-grade citations/as-of support, or miss required Companies House anchoring.

Q5.rationale: Most founding years/cohorts are correct but citations are weak and several required origin details are missing. Alphawave is a zero because the HQ is incorrectly given as London instead of Toronto despite the explicit 2017 anchor.

Q6.rationale: The broad stage taxonomy is partly captured, but several dominant stages are wrong or under-specified, product evidence/citations are missing, and collision-zone intensity is incomplete or mislabeled, especially stage 7 and post-Ansys multiphysics.

Q7.rationale: The as-of date and market values are not aligned to the benchmark, several EV bridges and multiples are materially off, and structural events are mishandled. The over/under conclusions are directionally right, but most per-entity valuation mechanics are outside tolerance.

Q8.rationale: The answer fabricates or misstates key customer concentration disclosures for Synopsys and Cadence and misses Arm China/Qualcomm specifics. Scenario arithmetic and contribution-margin assumptions are mostly wrong or absent, with only limited ND handling for private/segment entities.
